desc:
A prefix c of s covers s if every position of s lies inside at least one occurrence of c in s. Occurrences may overlap. The whole string always covers itself.

Return the length of the shortest covering prefix.

Examples: "abaababaab" is covered by "abaab" (occurrences at indices 0 and 5), so the answer is 5. "abababa" is covered by "aba" at indices 0, 2 and 4, so the answer is 3. "aabaaaab" has no shorter cover, so the answer is 8.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Testing every prefix length with a full search for its occurrences costs O(n<sup>2</sup>) or worse. Which prefixes can be covers at all?
A cover must start and end the string, so it is a border of s (or s itself). Its occurrences must also leave no gap: consecutive occurrence ends must be at most |c| apart.

Compute cover[i], the shortest cover of every prefix, in increasing i. For prefix i let c = cover[pi[i]]; this c also covers the prefix of length i if the previous occurrence of the prefix of length c ended at most c positions before i. Remember last[c], the end of the latest occurrence.
editorial: Work on every prefix of s, not only on s. Let cover[L] be the length of the shortest covering prefix of the prefix s[0..L-1]; by default it is L itself. A covering prefix of a string is a border of it, so for prefix length L the only candidate that could be better than L is a cover of the longest border b = pi[L-1], namely c = cover[b] (a shorter border cannot do better than what the longest border already achieved).

The candidate c works for the prefix of length L if and only if it leaves no gap before the new occurrence that ends at L. Keep last[c], the end of the most recent occurrence of the prefix s[:c] that was used as a cover. If L - last[c] ≤ c, the new occurrence overlaps or touches the covered region, so set cover[L] = c and last[c] = L. Otherwise cover[L] = L and last[L] = L.

Answer cover[n]. Each prefix is handled in O(1) after the prefix function, so the algorithm is O(n) time and space. A brute-force check (mark all occurrences of each prefix and test full coverage) is O(n2) and is a good way to test your implementation.
